headline: The ferry has crossed: cruise saucers land in MISSILE COMMAND
lede: The weakest title on the shelf got its gap-1 saucer slice — a satellite-shaped craft that crosses the sky from wave 6, fires real warheads, and pays 125 if you burn it. Waves 1..5 replay byte-identical, so every old proof still stands.

notes.text: Missile Command wave 6+ now sends a seeded ferry across y 120–200 — one per wave, a second every three waves. Its missiles ride the exact warhead physics, so the WATCH gunner covers them with no doctrine change; the gunner itself only takes the bonus shot when every warhead is already covered and the craft is well over the board.

missilecmdcheck grew to 49 checks (+16 §saucers incl. byte-exact wave-1..5 trace pins) and 12 mutants, all dying. New mcsaucerdrive proves it in real Chrome: live wave-1 negative in probe AND pixels, sprite↔probe position match, a real mouse aim + Space pays +125 on the live board, zero page errors.

Fandom and StrategyWiki 403 the crawler; the Atari 1981 2600 manual on archive.org is the fetchable Atari-text source for the exotic-weapon rules (§2 look-like-satellites, §6 after-wave-6, Table 1 125 points) and matches the arcade article's wording — worth remembering for the next original-mechanics stage.

Starting a new mechanic at a wave above every existing proof's bar (wave 6 > sweep's 5, rollout's early waves) made the risky change free: gates by construction, pinned traces to prove it, QA polish filed at #3638, gap rest at #3630.
